Title: Optional Ant-Farm GIF Visualizer
Summary: Combine the Go replay decoder and raster studio into a pipeline consumer that writes an animated colony GIF and a text replay.
Overview:
Build visualizer, a Go-only consumer of valid lem-in stdout. It reads the echoed colony and ant movements from stdin, validates them, then writes an animated GIF showing ants travelling through the coordinate-defined colony. It also writes a legend and a text replay so the data remains reviewable without animation.

Reuse P13's immutable validated history and P14's mapper, raster primitives and GIF encoder. Core lem-in must already pass its own readiness gates. The bonus visualizes a schedule; it does not make a slow schedule optimal or repair an illegal one.

Feasible standard-library scope

GIF is the chosen rendering target because Go's standard library provides raster images and GIF encoding. An installed image viewer or browser can display the file without student JavaScript, a GUI toolkit or a third-party graphics package. A 3D visualizer is mentioned as an extra in the upstream audit, but is not required by this academy's optional 2D bonus.

Refresher:
Composition should keep parsing, simulation and rendering independent. P13 produces a validated history with room names, coordinates, tunnels and one position per ant at each boundary. P14 maps the fixed scene once and draws frames from those positions.

Interpolate only movement positions between validated boundaries. An ant traverses the drawn tunnel from its old room to its new one; waiting ants stay fixed. Collocated start/end ants can be rendered as a deterministic compact cluster or an aggregate marker, while the companion text preserves every ID.

Preflight the whole output before large frame allocation. A GIF is binary output, so do not mix diagnostic text into it. This academy writes binary GIF to a named file and leaves stdout available for a concise file summary. Invalid input must not leave an apparently successful final GIF.

// Published interface after students finish both executables:
// ./lem-in ant-farm.txt | ./visualizer
// Result: farm.gif, legend.txt, replay.txt in the current directory.
Spec:
1. Compile the CLI as visualizer. With no arguments read stdin and write farm.gif, legend.txt and replay.txt. Optionally support -out path.gif, with companion files in the same selected directory.
  2. Decode the complete academy transcript using P13, independently validate legal movement and completion, and reject solver error output, malformed/truncated streams and Reader failures. A legal but suboptimal transcript can be visualized; label the output as a replay, never a proof of optimum.
  3. Draw every room and tunnel from the colony. Fit the supplied coordinates with P14's aspect-preserving transform, including negatives, zero spans and coincidences. Room identity is independent from coordinates.
  4. Use four interpolation frames per logical turn at the declared timing, plus initial/final holds. Draw ants moving along their actual tunnels; keep waiting/arrived ants represented. End on the actual all-end snapshot.
  5. Preserve names and every ant's identity in legend/replay text. If the image aggregates terminal ants or separates coincident markers for visibility, document that display policy and retain exact positions in the companion text.
  6. Keep all student code standard-library-only, with no browser script, third-party fonts, graphics library or external encoder. GIF, PNG and text files are generated by Go.
  7. Apply P13's input bounds and P14's frame, dimension and total-pixel bounds; check arithmetic before allocation. Return a distinct resource error without dropping turns, shrinking the requested dimensions silently or presenting a partial final GIF as success.
  8. Use temporary files in the destination directory while writing. Finalize only after encoding and closing succeed; clean up owned temporary files on failure. Do not overwrite an existing output set without an explicit documented -overwrite flag. Multi-file rename is not fully atomic: document cleanup and rollback behavior.
  9. On success stdout names the three files; diagnostics go to stderr and failures return nonzero. No auto-opening viewer is required. Include decode-back metadata tests, logical-boundary pixel checks, pipeline tests and actual visual inspection.

Components.Title: Connect the validated replay boundary
Components.Goal: Make the visualizer consume the same observable stream as an external reviewer.
Before: Does the renderer need to know how Lx-y tokens are spelled?
What happens if lem-in prints an invalid-data line?
Steps: Integrate P13 as a Reader-based input package.
Retain coordinates, tunnels, names and copied snapshots.
Validate output destinations and resource estimates before image allocation.
Components.Hint: Never bypass replay validation just because the producer is your own solver. Pipe fixtures should include a deliberately corrupted stream.
Components.Trace: Pass a valid echo and only half its movements. No final GIF or success message should remain.
Components.Gate: Valid, invalid-data, malformed, truncated and failing-reader streams have distinct tested outcomes.

Components.Title: Render a faithful colony and ant motion
Components.Goal: Keep the graphical story consistent with logical replay state.
Before: How will terminal crowds be shown without losing ant counts?
How do coincident coordinates affect visibility but not identity?
Steps: Map the static scene once and render all tunnels/rooms in stable order.
Choose a documented terminal/overlap display policy.
Render each interpolation frame from immutable old/new positions and preserve exact boundary frames.
Components.Hint: Use the text replay to check any visually ambiguous terminal crowd. The image is a display of state, not the authoritative identity store.
Components.Trace: Inspect a two-ant pipeline on s-a-t. At the middle boundary, one ant is at end and the other at a; a persistent trail must not suggest two ants share a.
Components.Gate: First, intermediate and final keyframes agree with independently decoded logical snapshots.

Components.Title: Write bounded outputs safely
Components.Goal: Avoid confusing failed or partial artifacts with successful visualization.
Before: When can output files be renamed to final paths?
What happens if the second companion write fails?
Steps: Check destination collisions and require explicit overwrite policy.
Encode and close owned temporary outputs, tracking every error.
Finalize the output set and document/implement cleanup if a later rename fails.
Components.Hint: Closing a file can fail too. Do not declare success immediately after gif.EncodeAll returns if later file operations are still pending.
Components.Trace: Inject a Writer that fails after a prefix. The final farm.gif path must not be presented as a completed artifact.
Components.Gate: Output collision, encode failure, close failure and finalization failure have deliberate outcomes.

Components.Title: Verify the real pipeline and animation
Components.Goal: Combine machine checks with a viewed replay.
Before: What can decode-back tests prove that visual inspection cannot?
Steps: Run the corridor fixture through stdin and decode the resulting GIF back in Go tests.
Compare frame count, delay array, dimensions and final ant positions.
Inspect desktop and mobile-sized image viewing plus legend/replay readability, recording the viewer used.
Components.Hint: Some viewers ignore tiny delays; the encoded metadata remains testable. This bonus uses 10-centisecond subframes to avoid relying on extremely short timing.
Components.Trace: For T=3, expect 4T+2=14 frames, initial/final delays 40 and twelve intermediate delays 10.
Components.Gate: The GIF visibly moves ants along tunnels, has no ghost trails, ends with all ants at end and has accurate companion text.

Run:
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build -o visualizer .
# Windows executable name: go build -o visualizer.exe .
# Unix, after building the completed solver:
# ./lem-in colony.txt | ./visualizer
# Windows PowerShell native pipeline:
# .\lem-in.exe colony.txt | .\visualizer.exe
# For byte-exact portable tests, connect processes with Go os/exec.
# POSIX shell fixture: go run . < testdata/transcript.txt
# PowerShell: use the Go os/exec test harness for exact input bytes.
Verification:
The fixture contains three turns, so expect 14 GIF frames at the configured four-subframe rate, with first/last holds of 40 centiseconds. All ants must end at t in replay.txt.

  • Corridor, two-branch colony, negative coordinates, zero-span axes and coincident rooms: all render without panic.
  • Hyphenated and UTF-8 names survive the legend; names need not fit inside a room marker.
  • Decode the output with gif.DecodeAll and compare frame dimensions, count, delays and final keyframe pixels.
  • Invalid solver output, truncated replay, bad move and resource breach: no final success artifact.
  • Existing output files without -overwrite: clear error and unchanged files.
  • Inspect real motion in a viewer; compare several logical boundaries with replay.txt, checking waits, terminal crowds and no trails.

Exit gate

Core L01 readiness remains separate. The optional bonus is review-ready only after a real pipeline, decode-back checks, failure cleanup tests and viewed animation pass. Record any untested shell/viewer combinations honestly.
Engineering: Why should a visualizer validate movement even when it consumes your own solver's stdout?
Can a beautiful animation mislead a reviewer about minimum turns?
How do you balance visual separation of coincident rooms with preserving supplied coordinates?
What is the simplest accessible representation of every ant when start/end contain many?
Why is multi-file output finalization more complicated than renaming one GIF?
What correctness claim survives when a viewer changes playback timing?
How would you extend the renderer while keeping the Go-only standard-library boundary?
Practical: Generate the corridor replay and inspect turn 2 against replay.txt.
Decode the GIF and assert 14 frames.
Add coincident room coordinates and document the display result.
Feed an invalid-data line through stdin.
Create an output collision and confirm original bytes remain unchanged.
Force a low pixel budget and confirm there is no success artifact.
Record the viewer and shell used for the final pipeline check.
Extras: Add a Go-generated PNG contact sheet alongside the GIF for static review.
Add numeric bitmap room IDs and ant IDs where space permits, retaining the text legend.
Add configurable turn duration with a documented rounding policy for GIF delays.
Render deterministic terminal clusters or count glyphs for large ant populations.
Explore a Go-only isometric projection using the same raster primitives as a stretch project; retain 2D replay correctness and do not add an unrequested graphics dependency.
